subject: Service degradation — consolidated post-incident summary & action playbook
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Denning <claire@elixirhealth.com>; ElixirHealth Ops <ops@elixirhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-28 09:15 PST
Subject: Service degradation — consolidated post-incident summary & action playbook

Hi Claire / Elixir team,

Thanks again for your patience this morning while we investigated the degraded inference latency you observed between 07:18–08:02 UTC. We've completed our internal synthesis and want to share a concise, customer-facing summary and the concrete actions we're committing to.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Impact: Elevated 99th percentile latency for text-generation requests on model variant rwd-v2-q4 between 07:18–08:02 UTC, affecting ~3% of requests for the ElixirHealth tenant. No data loss or wrong outputs were observed.
- Root cause (short): A bug in autoscaling priority reconciliation allowed a small set of GPU nodes to double-schedule long-running batches during a momentary resource pressure event, leading to head-of-line latency amplification.
- Immediate mitigation: We rolled a hotfix at 07:42 UTC that disabled the faulty reconciliation path and rebalanced queues; by 08:02 UTC 99p latency returned to nominal.

Attachments: post-incident-playbook.pdf (concise RCA + mitigation playbook), incident-timeline.csv (detailed event timestamps), mitigation-action-tracker.xlsx (owners + ETA).

What we are committing to for ElixirHealth:
1) Permanent fix: code change to the reconciliation algorithm + additional unit tests (owner: Marissa, ETA: 2027-03-07).
2) Runtime guard rails: deploy a short-circuit to prevent double-scheduling under resource pressure across Dedicated pools (owner: Jonas, ETA: 2027-03-03).
3) Monitoring & alerting: new 99p latency alert scoped to per-tenant variance and an automated rollback trigger for containers exceeding token-throttle thresholds (owner: Connor, ETA: 2027-03-01).
4) Postmortem review: share full technical write-up and remediation verification report.

We know operational disruption matters — we plan to issue a service credit for the window impacted. I'll have a proposed credit calculation and accounting steps in the next message once we align on scope.

If it helps, we can schedule a 30-minute call this afternoon to walk through the timeline and answer any technical questions. Are you available at 15:00 PST (23:00 UTC)?

Best,
Sooshin Lee
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Claire Denning <claire@elixirhealth.com>

Date: 2027-02-28 09:48 PST
Subject: Re: Service degradation — consolidated post-incident summary & action playbook

Thanks, Soojin — and thanks to your team for the quick investigation and the clear summary. A few quick questions:

1) Can you confirm whether any scheduled jobs from our side caused the resource pressure? We had a nightly batch that started at 07:10 UTC — not sure if it correlates.
2) Please share the proposed credit calculation. Our procurement/legal team will want the figure and the rationale.
3) We'd like to understand risk to model output quality if the runtime guard rails are applied (will they change sampling/config?).

15:00 PST works for me; if you can send a calendar invite I will forward to my infra lead.

—Claire
Director of Engineering, ElixirHealth

On Mon, Feb 28, 2027 at 09:15 Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai> wrote:

To: Claire Denning <claire@elixirhealth.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-28 11:02 PST
Subject: Re: Service degradation — consolidated post-incident summary & action playbook

Claire — appreciate the fast reply. Quick answers while we prepare the detailed artifacts: 

1) Correlation with Elixir nightly batch: We've instrumented tenant resource attribution and can confirm the event originated on Redwood's serving layer; the nightly job increased request load but did not independently cause scheduling conflicts — the defect in reconciliation meant the transient load amplified scheduling collisions. We'll include the request traces from your tenant in the full write-up (see incident-timeline.csv).

2) Credits: proposed customer-facing calculation: (duration of degraded window * % of affected requests * baseline token-unit cost) = estimated credit USD. For transparency, example calculation attached in mitigation-action-tracker.xlsx (tab: credits). We propose issuing a one-time usage credit to be applied on your next invoice. Accounting steps: we'll draft a formal credit memo and route to your AP contact once you confirm acceptance. (Owner: Marissa — ETA: credit memo draft by 2027-03-02).

3) Runtime guard rails impact on output: the short-circuit only affects scheduling and admission under resource pressure; it does not alter sampling parameters, quantization, or generation configuration. There will be no change to model hyperparameters for normal requests. We'll include a smoke test plan and customer-signed acceptance criteria in the mitigation tracker.

Action owners & immediate next steps (summary):
- Marissa: final technical write-up + credit memo proposal (ETA 2027-03-02)
- Jonas: deploy short-circuit to Dedicated pools and run canary (ETA 2027-03-03)
- Connor: add tenant-scoped 99p latency alert + rollback runbook (ETA 2027-03-01)
- Soojin: schedule recap call + share postmortem folder (today)

We will not change any inference configuration for your workloads without explicit sign-off.

Regards,
Marissa
Director, Product Reliability
Redwood Inference

Next steps before the call (please see attachments in the shared folder):
- Marissa will walk through the timeline and code-level root cause (post-incident-playbook.pdf).
- Jonas will present the guard-rail design and canary plan.
- Connor will review monitoring changes and the rollback playbook.

Wrap-up and commitments we will confirm on the call:
- Final credit amount and accounting process (Marissa owner).
- Acceptance criteria for the guard rails (Elixir and Redwood sign-off).
- Verification run and closure checklist to be executed after the canary.

If anything else is needed prior to the call, reply here or ping me directly. We'll follow up with the full technical appendices after the meeting and mark the thread resolved once all items are complete.

Appreciate your partnership — we'll be ready to walk through everything end-to-end.

Best,
